newsitem.title: CANADA: Newbridge shares see-saw after earnings.
newsitem.headline: Newbridge shares see-saw after earnings.

text.p: Newbridge Networks Corp shares see-sawed wildly on Wednesday following the release of the networking equipment company's second-quarter earnings after market close on Tuesday.

Newbridge profits were just a penny shy of consensus estimates and some analysts expressed concerns about the company's performance next quarter. Brokerage Alex. Brown cut its rating on Newbridge to a buy from a strong buy.
"I think people...have some questions here because there appears not to be a lot of upside for the coming quarter," said Wojtek Uzdelewicz, an industry analyst at Cowen & Co.
"(In addition) they didn't beat the street with their numbers this quarter and the street is a little bit spoiled," Uzdelevicz added.
But long-term, most observers were still optimistic.
"I think longer-term, these guys are very well-positioned. We continue to be very bullish on them. But this quarter (coming up), don't look for a lot of upside," Uzdelevicz said.

Dillon Read and Co reiterated their buy recommendation this morning. "There were no negative issues in the quarter. There was good fundamental growth across all their product areas," said Robert MacLellan.
"We reiterated our buy this morning. We suggested that any softness on the open this morning, clients should see as a buying opportunity," MacLellan said.

The rounding of decimals after the recent stock split and the currency exchange worked against Newbridge this quarter, MacLellan said. But he said speculators who breeze through an income statement and focus only on the bottom line sold the stock at the open because the earnings were slightly short of expectations. But fundamental players stepped in soon after.
Newbridge shares swung wildly, falling as low as 42.25 and climbing as high as 46.20 on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
They were up 0.25 at 44.65 early afternoon. In New York, Newbridge fell to 31-3/8 early and then spiked to 34-3/8 before settling back to trade 1/8 higher at 33-1/4.
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com
